findings.title: One-quarter of Gaza households headed by women face mounting humanitarian needs, UN warns
findings.publisher: WAFA Palestinian News & Information Agency (reporting UN Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq's 19 November briefing)
findings.affected_population_system: Children dependent on temporary learning sites; displaced households relying on emergency education services
findings.source_type: Established regional news agency's attributed report of a United Nations spokesperson's briefing; UN original not accessible in this check
findings.incident_summary: A November 20 WAFA report of UN Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq's November 19 briefing states that flash flooding earlier in November damaged approximately 200 temporary learning sites, close to one-third of operating educational facilities in Gaza. This is retrospective and provides a newer damage figure for education infrastructure, not an incident during the observation hour.
findings.exact_supporting_passage: flash floods caused by rainfall earlier this month damaged around 200 temporary learning sites across Gaza

discovery_context.method: Targeted WAFA search followed by full primary-agency article read; compared with OCHA OPT 13 November report and prior verified watch heartbeat
discovery_context.novelty_basis: Preceding heartbeat logged crossing figures only. WAFA/UN briefing's approximately 200 damaged temporary learning sites adds a distinct quantified infrastructure-damage follow-up to OCHA 13 November's statement that over 100 learning spaces became inaccessible; the two measures differ and are not additive.
discovery_context.source_publication_local: 2026-11-20 10:02 AM (WAFA website; timezone not explicitly verified)
discovery_context.corroboration: WAFA attributes its account to named UN Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq. Original UN press briefing blocked by anti-bot/JavaScript; independently verifying the exact 200 figure was not possible.
discovery_context.caution: Do not treat as newly damaged during November 20, double count the earlier OCHA learning-space disruption, or infer that all 200 sites ceased operating.
